weekly.summary: The department argued in a court filing that OpenAI legally used articles by The New York Times to develop A.I., adding that national security depended on American tech dominance.

weekly.title: Trump’s Tactics to Lower Beef Prices and Appease Ranchers Fall Short
weekly.summary: The Agriculture Department offered new initiatives for ranchers after President Trump said he would import more beef. The moves aren’t a quick fix.

weekly.title: The ‘Miracle House’ That Survived Nepal’s Floods
weekly.summary: People are coming to take photos of the green-painted house, which kept the Pyakurel family safe as the area all around them was destroyed by rampaging floodwaters.

weekly.title: Uber Lays Off 10% of Employees in Sweeping Reorganization
weekly.summary: The layoffs affect about 3,300 workers, as Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi bets on a “leaner organization.”

weekly.title: Putin and Iran 'need each other desperately,' expert says, as Russia voices support for regime
weekly.summary: Vladimir Putin declared full solidarity with Iran as an expert said both nations "need each other desperately" during the escalating U.S.-Iran conflict.

weekly.title: U.S. and Iran Survey the Damage After a Night of Intense Strikes
weekly.summary: The American military said its barrage was retaliation against recent attacks on U.S. forces and marine traffic. Iranian officials said a wedding was hit and civilians killed.

weekly.title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
weekly.summary: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.

weekly.title: Thai resort city cracks down on prostitution ahead of USS Abraham Lincoln arrival
weekly.summary: Pattaya police ramped up patrols and raids ahead of the USS Abraham Lincoln's arrival, arresting over 50 people as 5,000 sailors hit the resort city.

weekly.title: In Nepal and Tibet, Pollution on Glaciers Could Fuel More Flood Disasters
weekly.summary: Darkened by soot from vehicles and factories, the region’s glaciers are absorbing more heat and melting at dangerous rates.

weekly.title: FiveThirtyEight’s Podcast Hosts Reunite for a New Show
weekly.summary: Nate Silver, Clare Malone and Galen Druke will host “Still Counting,” a nonpartisan politics show — on a decidedly partisan podcast network.

weekly.title: Rescuers use ziplines to transport trapped citizens after devastating Nepal floods decimate country's bridges
weekly.summary: Video shows rescue workers using cable cars and ziplines to ferry stranded citizens across flooded rivers in Nepal after the deadly mudslide.

weekly.title: Trump revives Iran regime change speculation with cryptic call for people to 'rise up'
weekly.summary: Trump asking when Iranians will “rise up and fight" revives questions over whether the administration’s Iran strategy is shifting beyond economic pressure and negotiations

weekly.title: Two More Oil Tankers Are Attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
weekly.summary: The ships were hit near Oman on Monday, the latest attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf. Oil prices rose more than 2 percent.

weekly.title: In Egypt, Xi Challenges America’s Influence in the Middle East
weekly.summary: China’s leader, Xi Jinping, is seeking to deepen ties with a longtime U.S. security partner and to project a larger role for Beijing in a region rocked by war.

weekly.title: Chevron Expansion in Venezuela Extends U.S. Influence Over Oil Riches
weekly.summary: The U.S. energy giant, which stayed in the country after other Western companies left, will invest $7 billion in the country to more than double its production there.

weekly.title: Employer Health Costs Are Expected to Spike in 2027
weekly.summary: A new U.S. survey anticipates an average increase of 11 percent unless benefits are cut, the highest rate in decades. Other findings also predict a sharp rise.

weekly.title: Global Bond Rates Are Rising. What Should You Do Now?
weekly.summary: If you own bonds, they may be in a broad fund that hasn’t lost much money. And that fund may do much better in the next several years.

weekly.title: Status of Iran’s Nuclear Program Is Unclear, U.N. Watchdog Says
weekly.summary: As the war sputters on, an internal report from the International Atomic Energy Agency said Iran’s refusal to grant access to its inspectors was an urgent concern.

weekly.title: Saturday Evening Post Will Stop Printing After 205 Years
weekly.summary: The magazine, famous for publishing Jack London stories and Norman Rockwell art, will continue online.

weekly.title: Bill Simmons’s Co-Hosts Are Tired of His A.I. Antics
weekly.summary: The founder of The Ringer is taking flak for using artificial intelligence to conjure opinions from the deceased film critic Roger Ebert. Ads from OpenAI have recently run on the show.

weekly.title: Raging inferno erupts at Bali beachside restaurant party
weekly.summary: Video shows flames engulfing a restaurant in Bali, Indonesia, after a reported balloon explosion during a birthday party sparked a massive inferno.

weekly.title: Explosion near German train station injures 2 Ukrainian citizens
weekly.summary: Two Ukrainian citizens suffered minor injuries in the Augsburg train station explosion as police investigate a possible motive amid rising tensions.

weekly.title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
weekly.summary: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.

weekly.title: At G20 Meeting, Scott Bessent Accuses China of Flooding the World With Cheap Exports
weekly.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused China for flooding the world with its cheap exports.

weekly.title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
weekly.summary: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.

weekly.title: Map Apps Are Handling Trump’s Renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America Differently
weekly.summary: Navigation companies face a new dilemma after President Trump ordered Lake Ontario to be renamed Lake America.

weekly.title: Germany blames Russia after explosive-laden drone found near Ukrainian cargo planes at major airport
weekly.summary: Germany closed Russia's Bonn consulate after linking Moscow to a failed drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport targeting a Ukrainian cargo aircraft.

weekly.title: Bond Sell-Off Threatens to Squeeze Borrowers Around the World
weekly.summary: Government bond yields are hitting multi-decade highs, reflecting anxiety about debt levels, deficits and inflation. The effects will extend to mortgages, business loans and other types of credit.

weekly.title: One glaring issue goes unaddressed in UN chief's high-stakes talks with Iran's president
weekly.summary: António Guterres met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, but a U.N. readout omitted any mention of detained protesters or torture allegations.

weekly.title: US embassies in Middle East warn Americans of 'unforeseen escalation' as latest strikes hit Iran
weekly.summary: Multiple U.S. embassies warned Americans in the Middle East to "exercise caution and heightened vigilance," while CENTCOM launched fresh strikes on Iran.

weekly.title: What to Know About Venezuelan Energy Following Trump’s Oil Deal
weekly.summary: The Trump administration’s deal with a private oil company to increase oil production in the South American country could take many years to come to fruition.

weekly.title: Ozempic Maker Novo Nordisk’s Investors Are Nervously Looking Into the Future
weekly.summary: Novo Nordisk’s chief executive, Mike Doustdar, is a year into a corporate turnaround. He says investors are still underestimating the promise of the company’s drugs.

weekly.title: Locals torch migrant shelters as Spain's PM points blame beyond the border
weekly.summary: Ceuta residents burned migrant shelters as Pedro Sánchez accused Russian and Israeli-linked networks of spreading disinformation that fueled the crisis.

weekly.title: Israel captures top Hamas commander in Gaza strike, defense minister says
weekly.summary: Israel Katz says IDF forces captured Hamas security chief Mu'in al-Arabid during a deep raid in Gaza, with airstrikes covering the withdrawal.

weekly.title: Satsuki Katayama, the Woman at the Center of Japan’s Currency Fight
weekly.summary: Japan’s finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, is under pressure to strengthen the yen while balancing competing demands from the prime minister and Washington.

weekly.title: Trump says Iran is ‘DEAD’ — experts point to the real sign Tehran is nearing the brink
weekly.summary: U.S. strikes on Iranian launchers near the Strait of Hormuz triggered ballistic missile retaliation as Brent crude climbed above $90 a barrel Monday.

weekly.title: John Ternus Replaces Tim Cook as Apple CEO
weekly.summary: Big technology and management changes are greeting John Ternus, whose long-serving predecessor, Tim Cook, will stay on as executive chair.

weekly.title: Roughly 80 Americans still unaccounted for after Himalayan disaster kills 903, officials say
weekly.summary: Nepal and China's death toll climbed to 903 as roughly 4,200 people remained unaccounted for following the devastating flood and debris flow.

weekly.title: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Advertising Practices
weekly.summary: Regulators say the e-commerce giant forced more than a million advertisers to pay more than they should have. The company denies the claims.

weekly.title: New report exposes intact Iranian bunker that may hide regime's ongoing nuclear work
weekly.summary: The bunkered Natanz structure was built between 2010 and 2017, raising urgent questions about Iran's uranium enrichment capabilities after two wars.

weekly.title: Putin unleashes new fury on Ukraine as report exposes fear hanging over war’s end
weekly.summary: Russia launched nearly 1,500 drones in four days as Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Moscow aims to exhaust Ukraine, with daytime attacks now disrupting Kyiv.

weekly.title: Parkgoer airlifted after Batman roller coaster incident leaves man with fractures to both legs
weekly.summary: A 49-year-old visitor was airlifted to a hospital after suffering fractures in both legs on a Batman-themed roller coaster in Spain, lcoal reports say.

weekly.title: Nicolás Maduro flashes peace signs in first prison photos since US capture in Caracas
weekly.summary: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in his first photos from a New York prison, smiling as he awaits trial on federal drug trafficking charges.

weekly.title: Influencers Have a Lot to Say About Politics. Many Are Quietly Paid for It.
weekly.summary: Their videos have proliferated on social media, but the payments are frequently hidden from viewers.

weekly.title: How Meta’s $17.1 Billion Social Media Settlement Came Together
weekly.summary: State attorneys general spent months in negotiations. Then, as its legal losses mounted, the social media giant’s new top lawyer brought a huge settlement to the table.
